q0921: The Korba Super Thermal Power Station (NTPC) is in Chhattisgarh's Korba coalfield, which is why Korba is called the 'power capital' of India.
On the map of India, where would the Korba Thermal Power Plant be located?
q0924: GNP stands for Gross National Product: GDP plus net factor income from abroad.
In national income accounting, GNP is the abbreviation used for __________.
q0926: Herbert Charles Brown first reported the hydroboration–oxidation reaction in the late 1950s; he shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for boron chemistry.
Hydroboration gives anti-Markovnikov alcohols from alkenes.
Who first reported the hydroboration–oxidation reaction in the late 1950s?
q0927: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi, the last Lodi Sultan of Delhi, at the First Battle of Panipat (1526), founding the Mughal Empire.
In 1526, the Mughal Empire was established in India after Babur defeated which ruler of the Delhi Sultanate?
q0929: The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 (in force 1995) gave Lok Adalats statutory status; their awards are final and binding.
Article 39A (free legal aid) is the constitutional basis.
Under which Act have Lok Adalats been given statutory status?
q0934: N.G. Majumdar excavated Chanhudaro (Sindh) in 1931; it is the only Harappan city without a citadel and had a bead-making workshop.
Harappa: Daya Ram Sahni (1921); Mohenjo-daro: R.D. Banerji (1922).
Who excavated the site of Chanhudaro in 1931?
q0935: John Newlands (1865) proposed the Law of Octaves: when elements are arranged by atomic mass, every eighth element resembles the first, like musical notes.
Döbereiner's triads (1817) came earlier; Mendeleev's periodic table (1869) later.
Which classification method was proposed by J.A.R. Newlands?
q0936: Outsourcing, where firms hire outside or overseas agencies for services such as call centres and IT, is a major outcome of globalisation.
India became a hub for BPO and IT outsourcing after 1991.
Outsourcing is one of the important outcomes of which process?
q0938: The First Battle of Panipat (1526), where Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi, ended the Lodi dynasty and began Mughal rule.
Khanwa (1527) against Rana Sanga secured Mughal rule.
Which event, which took place in 1526, marked the end of the Lodi dynasty and the beginning of Mughal rule?
q1022: Vijayalaya founded the imperial Chola dynasty around 850 CE by capturing Thanjavur. Dantidurga founded the Rashtrakutas; Gopala and Dharmapala were Palas.
Vijayalaya → Aditya I → Parantaka I → ... Rajaraja I.
Who among the following was the founder of the Imperial Chola Dynasty?
q1024: Structural unemployment comes from a mismatch between workers' skills and the jobs available when the economy's structure changes, e.g. technology or new industries.
Seasonal = off-season farm work; cyclical = recessions; frictional = between jobs.
What causes structural unemployment in the context of India?
q1028: Article 263 lets the President set up an Inter-State Council if public interest needs it; it is not permanent, advisory only, and does not decide river water disputes (Article 262 covers those). One was set up in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's advice.
Which of the following statements regarding the Inter-State Council under Article 263 is CORRECT?
q1029: Article 243Q: a Nagar Panchayat is for an area in transition from rural to urban, a Municipal Council for a smaller urban area, and a Municipal Corporation for a larger urban area.
Added by the 74th Amendment (1992), Part IXA.
According to the Constitution of India, which of the following pairs of urban bodies and their corresponding areas is CORRECTLY matched?
q1033: Oxygen binds to haemoglobin reversibly: it attaches in the lungs, forming oxyhaemoglobin, and is released in the tissues.
Carbon monoxide binds far more tightly, which is why it is poisonous.
The bond between oxygen and haemoglobin is _________.
q1034: The Qutub Minar (about 73 m) in Mehrauli, Delhi, begun by Qutbuddin Aibak and completed by Iltutmish, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1993).
Delhi's three UNESCO sites: Qutub Minar, Red Fort, Humayun's Tomb.
The Qutub Minar, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in which Indian city?
q1035: Tilka Manjhi (Jabra Paharia) led an early tribal revolt against the British in the Rajmahal hills of Bihar (now Jharkhand) in 1784–85; he was hanged in 1785.
He is often called the first Adivasi rebel against the British.
When did Tilka Manjhi start the Manjhi Revolt against the British regime in Bihar?
q1076: At Independence about 70–75% of India's workforce depended on agriculture, which was largely stagnant and low in productivity.
Agriculture still employs about 45% of India's workforce.
At the time of Independence, how was India's population primarily dependent on agriculture?
q1078: The Thar desert has sand dunes (barchans, seif dunes) and playas, shallow salt lakes such as Sambhar that fill in the rains.
Which of the following landforms are commonly found in the Great Indian Desert?
q1079: Lord Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse annexed states whose rulers died without a natural male heir: Satara (1848), Jhansi, Nagpur (1854) and others.
Subsidiary Alliance was Wellesley's; Permanent Settlement was Cornwallis's.
Which policy was introduced by Lord Dalhousie for annexing Indian states?
q1082: The Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar, given by the Sangeet Natak Akademi since 2006, honours young artists aged up to 40 in music, dance and drama.
Named after the shehnai maestro, a Bharat Ratna (2001).
'Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar' is given to Indian artists up to __________ of age.
q1083: The English daily 'Bande Mataram' began in August 1906 with Bipin Chandra Pal as editor; Aurobindo Ghosh soon took over and made it the voice of the Extremists.
Lal-Bal-Pal: Lajpat Rai, Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal.
An English newspaper titled Bande Mataram began publication in August 1906; which among the following personalities initially took charge as its editor?
q1086: The Vesara style, developed under the later Chalukyas and Hoysalas in the Deccan, combines the Nagara (northern) and Dravida (southern) temple styles.
Nagara = north, Dravida = south, Vesara = mix (Deccan).
The Vesara style of temple architecture is a fusion of which two architectural styles?
q1088: The south-west monsoon winds blow from the south-west towards the north-east over peninsular India, from the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal towards land.
Arabian Sea branch hits the Western Ghats first.
During the Southwest Monsoon season, in which direction do the monsoon winds primarily blow over the peninsular region?
q1089: The Indian Councils Act, 1892 increased non-official members in the Central and Provincial Legislative Councils (with an official majority kept) and let members discuss the budget and ask questions.

Which Act enlarged the participation of non-official members in the Central and Provincial Legislative Councils while keeping an official majority, and allowed the councils to debate the budget and question the executive?
q1092: Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva, 1989) was built to relieve congestion at Mumbai port; it is India's largest container port.
Kandla was similarly built to make up for losing Karachi.
Which port in India has been developed to relieve pressure on Mumbai port?
q1093: Forward genetics starts from an observed trait (phenotype) and works back to find the genes responsible; reverse genetics starts from a gene.
Forward: trait → gene. Reverse: gene → trait.
Forward genetics is especially useful for identifying __________.
q1275: Electromagnetic waves (light, radio, X-rays) need no medium and travel through a vacuum at 3 × 10⁸ m/s; sound needs a medium.
That is why we see the Sun but cannot hear it.
Unlike sound waves, electromagnetic waves can travel through ____________.
q1276: After Muhammad Ghori's death in 1206, his slave-general Qutbuddin Aibak became ruler of his Indian territories, founding the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty.
In which year did Qutbuddin Aibak become the ruler of Muhammad Ghori's Indian territories?
q1279: Article 24 prohibits employing children below 14 in factories, mines or other hazardous work.

Which Article among the Fundamental Rights prohibits the employment of children in factories, stating that 'no child below the age of fourteen years shall be employed to work in any factory or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment'?
q1281: Pulses (dal) are an incomplete protein: they lack enough of the amino acid methionine, which is why dal is eaten with rice or roti. Milk, eggs and fish are complete proteins.
Dal + rice together give all essential amino acids.
Which of the following is an incomplete protein (a protein source that does not contain all essential amino acids in sufficient amounts)?
q1283: Teak is the most important species of India's tropical deciduous (monsoon) forests, along with sal, sandalwood and bamboo.
Tropical deciduous forests are India's most widespread forest type.
Teak is the most prominent species of which type of forest in India?
q1288: Alauddin Khalji built Siri, the second city of Delhi, around 1303 as his capital, partly to defend against Mongol raids.
Seven cities of Delhi: Lal Kot, Siri, Tughlaqabad, Jahanpanah, Ferozabad, Dinpanah, Shahjahanabad.
Which city was built as the capital of Alauddin Khalji?
